mainTopic: Counting years: the kingdoms of the second בית המקדש, the scribes' count versus the count from the חורבן, and the world's six thousand years
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוסי's ברייתא that lists the kingdoms that ruled while the second בית המקדש stood: פרס 34 years, יון 180, חשמונאי 103, and בית הורדוס 103. After that, years are counted from the חורבן. The גמרא notes that this puts the start of Roman involvement 206 years before the חורבן, while an earlier teaching said Rome ruled for 180. It answers that for the first 26 years Rome was a loyal ally and did not rule over Israel. רב פפא then gives a trick for linking two ways of counting years. A תנא counting from the חורבן adds 20 to the scribe's year to recover his exact count, and a scribe subtracts 20 from the תנא's count. Next, תנא דבי אליהו teaches that the world lasts six thousand years: two thousand empty, two thousand of תורה, and two thousand of ימות המשיח, some of which have already passed because of our sins. The גמרא shows that the תורה block starts with אברהם in חרן, not at מתן תורה, a gap of 448 years. Finally, רב פפא says that to recover the exact count of משיח years that have passed, one adds forty-eight to the scribe's year. His memory sign comes on the next amud.

steps.title: How long each kingdom ruled while the second בית המקדש stood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the years of each kingdom during the second בית המקדש: פרס 34, יון 180, חשמונאי 103, הורדוס 103. After the חורבן, years are counted from the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Persian kingdom ruled 34 years while the Temple stood. The Greek kingdom ruled 180 years while the Temple stood. The Hasmonean kingdom ruled 103 years while the Temple stood. The Herodian kingdom ruled 103 years. From then on, go and count how many years it is after the destruction of the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא, a teaching of רבי יוסי, that divides the 420 years of the second בית המקדש into four ruling kingdoms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Add them up: 34 + 180 + 103 + 103 = 420 years, the full time the second בית המקדש stood. Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, the counting system switches, and years are counted from the חורבן. This timeline is the base for the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: While the בית המקדש was standing (literally 'in front of the House')
The Hasmonean family (the חנוכה heroes and their descendants)
The destruction of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Persian kingdom, while the Temple stood:
thirty-four years;
the Greek kingdom, while the Temple stood:
one hundred and eighty years;

phrases.aramaic: מַלְכוּת חַשְׁמוֹנַאי בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת מֵאָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: the Hasmonean kingdom, while the Temple stood: one hundred and three;
the kingdom of the house of Herod: one hundred and three.
From here onward, go out and calculate
how many years it is after the destruction of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְכוּת פָּרַס בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאַרְבַּע שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יוסי begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 420 years of the second בית המקדש divide into פרס 34, יון 180, חשמונאי 103, and הורדוס 103. After that, years are counted from the חורבן.

steps.title: 206 years or 180 years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that this timeline gives 206 years from the end of Greek rule to the חורבן. That clashes with an earlier statement that Rome ruled over Israel for 180 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently it was 206 years! But you said it was 180 years!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees a contradiction between the numbers in this ברייתא and an earlier statement about how long Rome ruled over Israel before the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After Greek rule ended came the Hasmonean 103 years and the Herodian 103 years, which adds up to 206 years before the חורבן. Yet an earlier teaching said the 'wicked kingdom', Rome, spread over Israel 180 years before the חורבן. The two numbers do not match, so the גמרא asks how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But you said (pointing to an earlier statement that seems to clash)

phrases.english: Evidently it was two hundred and six years,
phrases.notes: That's the 103 Hasmonean years plus the 103 Herodian years, from the end of Greek rule until the חורבן.

phrases.english: but you said it was one hundred and eighty!
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier teaching that Rome ruled over Israel for 180 years before the חורבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מָאתַן וְשֵׁית הֲווֹ, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a number out of step 1's timeline and sets it against an earlier statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that Rome ruled over Israel for 180 years before the חורבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי יוסי's timeline, 206 years passed between the end of Greek rule and the חורבן, not 180.

steps.title: Rome was a loyal ally for the first 26 years
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that for 26 years the Romans kept faith with Israel and did not rule over them. So those years are not counted as years of Roman rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for twenty-six years they stood faithfully with Israel and did not subjugate them. Therefore he does not count those years as part of the time when the wicked kingdom spread over Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: both numbers are right, but they measure different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rome's relationship with Israel began 206 years before the חורבן. For the first 26 years, though, Rome was a faithful ally and did not rule over Israel. Actual Roman rule over Israel lasted only 180 years (206 − 26 = 180).

keyTerms.meaning: In their faithfulness, keeping their word
They subjugated, they ruled harshly over

steps.whatToRemember: 206 years of Roman involvement minus 26 years of loyal alliance equals 180 years of real Roman rule over Israel.

phrases.english: Rather, for twenty-six years
they stood in their faithfulness with Israel,
and did not subjugate them;

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמְּטוּ לְהָכִי לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
phrases.english: and because of this he does not count them
as part of when the wicked kingdom spread over Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עֶשְׂרִין וְשֵׁית שְׁנִין קָמוּ בְּהֵימָנוּתַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what is being counted: an alliance period versus a period of rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both numbers seem to measure the same time of Roman rule, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: 206 counts from the start of the Roman connection. 180 counts only the years Rome actually ruled over Israel, leaving out 26 years of faithful alliance.

steps.title: A תנא who lost count: ask a scribe and add twenty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says a תנא who counts from the חורבן but forgot the exact number can ask a scribe for the year written in documents and add 20. Memory sign: 'These twenty years I have been in your house.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If this תנא made a mistake and doesn't know the details of how many years it has been, let him ask a scribe how many years he writes, add twenty years to that, and he will find his number. Your memory sign is: 'These twenty years I have been in your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new, practical point that grows out of the ברייתא: how to move between two ways of counting years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא counts years from the חורבן. The scribes, in their documents, use a different count that starts earlier. רב פפא says the תנא who remembers roughly where he is but not the exact details can take the scribe's number and add 20 to recover the details of his own count. The פסוק about 'twenty years' helps him remember that the number is twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: A scribe who writes documents (שטרות) and dates them
Your memory sign, a hint to help you remember

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תנא' does not mean a sage of the משנה. It means someone who counts years from the חורבן, as the ברייתא just taught.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If this tanna errs,
phrases.notes: This is the person who counts years from the חורבן.

phrases.english: and does not know the details of how many it has been,
let him ask the scribe how many years he writes,
and let him add twenty years to them,
and he will find his number.
And your memory sign:
"These twenty years I have been in your house."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי טָעֵי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's instruction to count from the חורבן, adding a practical trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who counts from the חורבן finds his year by taking the scribe's number and adding 20.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties together the count from the חורבן and the count used in documents, which matters for dating שטרות correctly.

steps.title: A scribe who lost count: ask a תנא and subtract twenty
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case: a scribe who forgot asks the תנא for his count and subtracts 20. Memory sign: the scribe takes away, the תנא adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the scribe made a mistake, let him ask the תנא how many years he counts, subtract twenty years from that, and he will find his number. Your memory sign: the scribe takes away, the תנא adds on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his trick by giving the reverse direction, for the scribe, along with a second memory sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the previous step. Since the תנא gets his number by adding 20 to the scribe's, the scribe gets his by subtracting 20 from the תנא's. The memory sign plays on words: 'תנא תוספאה' sounds like a תנא who teaches the תוספתא, but here it means 'the תנא adds'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who adds on (also hints at the תוספתא)

steps.whatToRemember: תנא (counting from the חורבן) = scribe's number + 20. Scribe = תנא's number − 20. Sign: 'ספרא בצירא, תנא תוספאה'.

phrases.english: If the scribe errs,
let him ask the tanna how many years he counts,
and let him subtract twenty years from them,
and he will find his number.
And your memory sign: the scribe subtracts,
the tanna adds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי טָעֵי סָפְרָא נְשַׁיְּילֵיהּ לְתַנָּא כַּמָּה חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's statement with the reverse direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scribe finds his year by taking the תנא's count and subtracting 20.

steps.title: The world's six thousand years in three blocks
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו teaches that the world exists for six thousand years: two thousand of emptiness, two thousand of תורה, and two thousand of ימות המשיח. Because of our sins, some of the משיח years have already passed without משיח coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage from the school of אליהו taught: The world lasts six thousand years. Two thousand are empty, two thousand are תורה, and two thousand are the days of משיח. Because of our many sins, some of those משיח years have already gone by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about counting years: a big map of world history split into three blocks of two thousand years each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first block is called 'empty' because the world did not yet have תורה. The second block is the time of תורה. The third block is meant for משיח, but our sins have let some of those years pass without him coming.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of אליהו

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-block map sets up the next question. Once we have a block called 'two thousand years of תורה,' we need to know exactly where it starts.

phrases.english: A Sage of the school of Eliyahu taught:
The world exists for six thousand years.
Two thousand years of emptiness,
phrases.notes: 'Emptiness' here means the world did not have תורה yet.

phrases.english: two thousand years of Torah,
two thousand years of the days of the Mashiach.
Because of our many sins
whatever years have gone out of them have gone out.
phrases.notes: He means some of the משיח years have already passed and משיח still has not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of counting years (steps 1-5) with a new teaching about the whole span of world history.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world lasts 6000 years: 2000 of emptiness, 2000 of תורה, and 2000 of ימות המשיח, some of which have already been lost because of our sins.

steps.title: When do the two thousand years of תורה begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks from what point the two thousand years of תורה are counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two thousand years of תורה: from when are they counted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the teaching it just quoted. This sets up the next move, where it tests one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching said there are two thousand years of תורה, but it did not say when they start. The גמרא needs a starting point that makes the numbers add up.

keyTerms.meaning: The two thousand years of תורה

phrases.english: The two thousand years of Torah: from when are they counted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the starting point of the middle block in the teaching from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting point of the two-thousand-year period of תורה.

steps.title: It cannot start at מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה years began at מתן תורה, the numbers would not fit, because more than two thousand years had already passed from creation by then.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they are counted from מתן תורה until now, there is not enough room for all of them. When you add up the years, you find that by מתן תורה it was already two thousand years plus part of the next thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the obvious answer, that the תורה years start at מתן תורה, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתן תורה happened more than two thousand years after creation. If the תורה block only started then, the 'empty' block would be longer than two thousand years, and the תורה block would run into the years that belong to משיח. So the obvious answer does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The giving of the תורה at סיני
There is not all that much (room)
You look into it, you calculate

steps.confusionAlert: The block of 'two thousand years of תורה' does NOT start at מתן תורה. That is exactly the answer the גמרא is rejecting here.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נֵימָא מִמַּתַּן תּוֹרָה עַד הַשְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: If we say from the giving of the Torah until now,
there is not all that much,
phrases.notes: He means there is not enough room for the full two thousand תורה years before the משיח block begins.

phrases.english: for when you look into them,

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי אַלְפֵי פְּרָטֵי דְּהַאי אַלְפָּא הוּא דַּהֲוַאי.
phrases.english: it was two thousand years plus some of this next thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא מִמַּתַּן תּוֹרָה עַד הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question in step 7 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting the תורה years from מתן תורה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By מתן תורה, more than 2000 years had already passed since creation, so the blocks would not line up.

steps.title: It starts from the souls made in חרן
steps.stepSummary: The תורה years start from the time אברהם and שרה brought people close to הקב״ה in חרן. By tradition, אברהם was fifty-two then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they are counted from 'And the souls that they made in חרן.' And we have a tradition that אברהם was fifty-two years old at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real starting point: the time אברהם and שרה began teaching people in חרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אברהם and שרה started bringing people close to הקב״ה, תורה began to spread in the world, even before סיני. The tradition that אברהם was fifty-two then fixes this moment exactly at year 2000 from creation. So the תורה block starts right where the empty block ends.

keyTerms.meaning: The souls they made in חרן, meaning the people אברהם and שרה brought close to הקב״ה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'time of תורה' started with אברהם spreading the knowledge of הקב״ה, not only with the giving of the תורה at סיני.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מִ״וְּאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן״,
phrases.english: Rather, from "And the souls that they made in Charan,"
and we have a tradition
that Avraham at that time
was fifty-two years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִוְּאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 rejected מתן תורה as the start, this gives the correct starting point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה years start from the souls made in חרן, when אברהם was 52, which is exactly year 2000.

steps.title: The 448-year gap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calculates the difference between the two starting points. From the souls made in חרן until מתן תורה is 448 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many years short is the count that the תנא taught? There are 448 years. When you calculate from 'the souls they made in חרן' until מתן תורה, there are 448 years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by measuring the gap between the starting point it rejected and the starting point it chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you counted from מתן תורה, you would miss 448 years of the תורה block. That is the time from אברהם in חרן until סיני. Counting from חרן is what makes the three blocks of two thousand fit exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: The six thousand years are: 2000 empty, 2000 תורה, 2000 משיח. The תורה block starts from אברהם in חרן (year 2000), not from סיני. The gap between the two points is 448 years.

phrases.english: How many years are missing from what the Tanna taught?
phrases.notes: He means: how many years would we lose if we counted the תורה block from סיני instead of from חרן?

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים וּתְמָנְיָא שְׁנִין הָוְיָין,
phrases.english: There are four hundred forty-eight years.
When you look into it,

phrases.aramaic: מֵ״הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן״ עַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: from "the souls that they made in Charan" until the giving of the Torah

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מְאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים וּתְמָנְיָא שְׁנִין הָוְיָין.
phrases.english: there are four hundred forty-eight years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the starting point from step 9 to measure exactly how far off the rejected starting point from step 8 would be.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: From חרן to מתן תורה is 448 years, so the תורה block begins at year 2000, not at סיני.

steps.title: רב פפא's trick for counting the lost years
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that if a תנא wants to state how many משיח years have passed but does not know the exact number, he should ask a scribe what year he writes on documents and add forty-eight. He then introduces a memory sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If a תנא gets confused and does not know the exact number of years, he should ask a scribe what year he writes on his documents. Then he should add forty-eight to that number, and he will have his answer. And here is your memory sign:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a simple way to find out exactly how many of the משיח years have already passed. His last word, 'and your sign is', sets up a memory sign that the גמרא gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said only that 'some' משיח years were already lost, without giving a number. Scribes wrote a year on every document using their own count, so anyone could find that number. רב פפא's case is a תנא who knows roughly how many hundreds have passed but has lost the exact count. If he adds forty-eight to the scribe's number, he recovers that exact count, just as in step 4 with the twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: Its details. Here it means the exact count of years.

steps.confusionAlert: The forty-eight is not a number of years that passed. It is a correction that lines up the tens and ones of the scribe's count with the משיח count. The תנא is assumed to remember the hundreds and only needs the exact details (פרטי).
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the vague statement in step 6 ('some years have passed') into something anyone can work out by asking a scribe.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If a tanna gets confused
phrases.notes: This means the person reciting the teaching, who wants to say how many משיח years have already passed.

phrases.english: and does not know its details, how many it is
let him ask a scribe how many he writes
phrases.notes: Scribes wrote the year on every document, so they always knew the current year by their count.

phrases.english: and let him add forty-eight to them
and he will find his total
and your memory sign is:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי טָעֵי תַּנָּא וְלָא יָדַע פְּרָטֵיהּ כַּמָּה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the calculation of the תורה years in steps 7-10, רב פפא goes back to the end of the step 6 teaching, the משיח years that already passed, and shows how to count them exactly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תנא who forgot the exact count of משיח years that have passed recovers it by taking the scribe's year and adding forty-eight.
